the development of radiopharmaceuticals for the in vivo imaging of the dopamine transporter in humans.
the development of new, selective ligands for in vivo imaging with PET and SPECT.
the development and evaluation of new selective radioligands for the dopamine transporter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dopamine transporter in the human brain is located in the striatum, the nucleus accumbens and the substantia nigra, and not in the cortex or the cerebellum, as previously suggested by other investigators.

[11C]- or [123I]-PE2I should prove to be useful ligands for the in vivo imaging of the dopamine transporter with PET/SPECT.

the dopamine transporter in the human brain can be imaged with PET or SPEGT using [11C] and [123I]-labeled PE2I.
